entries.stanceLine: Backdrop favours downside breaks — UK GDP Monthly Estimate @ 07:00 BST today — pre-release breaks are positioning, not conviction.

signals.text: UK GDP Monthly Estimate @ 07:00 BST today — pre-release breaks are positioning, not conviction.
GBP is a crowded short — a short-squeeze higher in sterling is a latent slap for upside breaks (strong GBP weighs on FTSE).

entries.aiStanceLine: Due to a GDP print landing 60 minutes before cash open seeding pre-positioned volatility, crowded GBP shorts that could reverse and press FTSE lower on any sterling squeeze, and Brent already down -1.26% dragging two top-5 index weights, opening-range breaks in either direction carry elevated fakeout risk today.
aiBullets: GDP printed at 07:00 BST — 60 minutes before the ORB forms — meaning the 10,426–10,483 overnight range already partially prices the outcome; first breaks may exhaust rather than extend.
Brent -1.26% weighs directly on Shell and BP (top-5 index weights), giving the short side a fundamental anchor even before any ORB mechanics play out.

GBP COT net-short of -89,991 contracts is at the 89th percentile of 20-day positioning — a crowded short that can unwind sharply, sending sterling up and FTSE perversely lower via the sign-flip, threatening upside ORB breaks.

With 45% of the 126.3-point 14-day average daily range already used and no further scheduled data today, range budget supports a move but the GDP-driven pre-open noise argues for waiting for a clean ORB level retest before entry.
